title: Quantum Error Mitigation with Diffusion-Like Models
authors: Yuval Idan, Ofek Nourian, Elad Mentovich, Taylor L. Patti, Eliahu Cohen
abstract: Coupling between a quantum system and its environment causes decoherence by transferring information from the system to environmental degrees of freedom. When discretized in time, such interactions can be interpreted as sequences of weak measurements that provide an effective model of noisy quantum dynamics. Motivated by this picture, we propose an AI-assisted error-mitigation framework for quantum diffusion processes generated by sequential local weak measurements. The forward process progressively erases information from the input state through weak measurements performed in randomly selected Pauli bases, producing basis-dependent local dephasing and locally depolarizing dynamics on average. Machine-learning models are trained on exact synthetic density matrices to learn a channel- and distribution-specific denoising map and estimate the corresponding pre-noise state. We benchmark the approach on single-qubit states and separable and entangled multi-qubit registers. We also study distribution-dependent local-to-global reconstruction, in which local reduced density matrices are used to reconstruct the global state. This experimentally motivated setting relies on locally accessible information and is therefore compatible with noisy and distributed quantum systems. More broadly, the framework provides a hybrid classical-quantum approach for approximating non-unitary dynamics and mitigating coherence loss.
summary: The paper introduces an AI-assisted framework to mitigate quantum noise caused by environmental coupling, modeling the process as a diffusion-like trajectory. It trains neural networks on synthetic data from weak measurements to learn an effective inverse map that reconstructs the original quantum state from noisy observations. This offers a powerful hybrid classical-quantum approach for approximating non-unitary dynamics in noisy quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses quantum error mitigation by developing an AI-assisted framework to estimate the initial state of a quantum system corrupted by decoherence.
main_result: They propose using machine learning models (like U-Nets and Transformers) trained on synthetic data from weak measurements to learn an effective, non-unitary denoising map that approximates the inverse noisy evolution channel.
method: The core method involves training neural networks to map observed noisy density matrices ($ho_t$) back to their estimated pre-noise state ($ho_0$), mimicking classical diffusion model inversion techniques in a quantum context.
model_or_system: The system is an arbitrary quantum state undergoing decoherence modeled by sequential local weak measurements, which generate a quantum diffusion process. The framework treats the noise as a sequence of non-unitary operations.
key_observables: Reconstructed initial density matrix ($ho_0$), noisy intermediate states ($\{ho_t\}$), and the fidelity of reconstruction across single and multi-qubit registers.
important_parameters: Measurement strength parameter ($\epsilon$) and the noise process parameters derived from Pauli basis measurements.
main_assumptions: The inverse process is an approximation, not a strictly physical quantum channel; local measurement independence is assumed for global reconstruction; and post-processing filters are used to enforce density matrix constraints.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the forward noisy evolution via weak measurements and the AI model's role in approximating the reverse path from $\{ho_t\}$ back to $ho_0$, comparing global vs. local reconstruction capabilities.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical problem of decoherence via weak measurements, then draws an analogy to classical diffusion models, details the training process using various ML architectures (LSTM, ViT, U-Net), and concludes with rigorous mathematical filtering techniques for ensuring output validity.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, machine learning-driven methodology for tackling open quantum system dynamics in noisy environments, which is crucial for scaling up near-term quantum hardware by mitigating coherence loss.

An initial quantum state ρ0 is evolved through a sequence of weak-measurement-induced noisy channels, producing a trajectory of mixed states {ρt}T t=1. An AI model is trained to approximate the inverse channel and map each noisy intermediate state ρt back toward the original state ρ0. The upper panels show the forward noisy evolution and the reverse trajectory predicted by the trained model. FIG. 2: Example of the separable six-qubit denoising task. An input state evolves under a noisy quantum channel and is gradually degraded. The trained model receives the noisiest state, corresponding to the output of the noisy channel, and learns an effective inverse map that reconstructs the erased information. The reconstructed state achieves FGM > 0.99 for a sequence length of 15 steps.

FIG. 3: Example of the local-to-global inverse reconstruction task for a five-qubit quantum register, which constitutes the most challenging dataset considered in this work. The reconstruction is performed using the Vision Transformer model. The model receives as input the five single-qubit reduced density matrices obtained from the noisy global state and predicts the corresponding initial global density matrix.

FIG. 4: Configuration and local-to-global reconstruction results. (a) Example of a noisy local quantum-register input, together with the model prediction and the corresponding ground truth. The reconstructed state achieves FGM = 0.9449. (b) Reconstruction-FGM distribution on the held-out test set (n = 18,000 states).
